rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham's kin are plainly astray in idolatry, which conflicts with the prophets' teaching and reason: a deity must suffice its worshippers or be needy of their worship.
rows.anchor: أن الإله لا يكون إلا كافيا لمن يعبده , وإلا كان فقيرا إلى تأله كم يكفيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God showed Abraham the dominion of heaven and earth so he would know that worship of anything besides God is error and become firmly certain of monotheism.
rows.anchor: فيعلم أن كل من عبد غير الله صنم وغيره من قومه وغيرهم في ضلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham's contemplation advanced from knowledge by inference to certainty by sight and then to the fullest certainty.
rows.anchor: بعد علم اليقين على عين اليقين بل حق اليقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because heavenly bodies are visible to all and nobler than earthly objects, disproving their divinity disproves the divinity of earthly objects all the more.
rows.anchor: وهي أشرف من الأرضية , فإذا بطلت صلاحيتها للإلهية بطلت الأرضية من باب الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He glosses the night as covering and darkening; the shortened verb form intensifies the darkness, while the following preposition depicts night falling over Abraham.
rows.anchor: فلما جن } أي ستر وأظلم , وقصره - وإن كان متعديا - دلالة على شدة ظلام تلك الليلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The star had appeared or risen when Abraham saw it.
rows.anchor: رأى كوكبا } أي قد بزغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham's words can be read as either a statement or a question; he feigned affirmation to draw his audience into reflection and make them receptive to proof.
rows.anchor: الصالح لأن يكون خبرا واستفهاما , ليوهمهم أنه مخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Setting proves that a star changes and moves, so it is originated and contingent rather than divine; Abraham spoke in his own voice only to alert his audience, since God had made him certain.
rows.anchor: لأن الأفول حركة , والحركة تدل على حدوث المتحرك وإمكانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers setting as evidence over rising: setting more clearly signals the star's lost power and insignificance, whereas rising still carries honor and apparent authority.
rows.anchor: ولم يستدل بالطلوع لأنه - وإن كان حركة دالة على الحدوث والنقصان - شرف في الجملة وسلطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Different audiences grasp different force in the proof: learned people infer contingency and a necessary creator, middling people infer origination from motion, and ordinary people see loss of light and authority.
rows.anchor: فالخواص يفهمون من الأفول الإمكان , والممكن لا بد له من موجد واجب الوجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The argument also targets Abraham's Persian people, who believed a planet's influence weakens as it descends west; a true deity does not change.
rows.anchor: وخص الأفول أيضا لأن قومه الفرس كانوا منجمين , ومذهبهم أن الكوكب إذا كان صاعدا من المشرق إلى وسط السماء كان قويا عظيم التأثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This argument shows that religion is grounded in proof rather than imitation.
rows.anchor: وهذا الاستدلال برهان في أن أصل الدين مبني على الحجة دون التقليد

rows.speaker: الأزهري
rows.claim: Al-Azhari explains the moon's first appearance with bazigh and says the word may derive from splitting, as its light cleaves the darkness.
rows.anchor: بازغا } أي طالعا أول طلوعه ؛ قال الأزهري : كأنه مأخوذ من البزغ الذي هو الشق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The moon's statement this is my Lord follows Abraham's earlier rhetorical tactic.
rows.anchor: قال هذا ربي } دأبه في الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The star's setting had already unsettled the audience because they heard it was subject to events, so Abraham emphasizes his response.
rows.anchor: تأمل أن الكوكب محل الحوادث بالأفول قد طرق أسماعهم فخالج صدورهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham's plea shows guidance comes from God, not from someone else, the mere display of already-present proofs, or knowledge of inference he already possessed.
rows.anchor: فدل ذلك على أن الهداية ليست إلى غيره , ولا تحمل على نصب الأدلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is a stronger and more explicit repudiation of the heavenly bodies' divinity than the first statement, while remaining tactful toward opponents.
rows.anchor: فكانت هذه أشد من الأولى وأقرب إلى التصريح بنفي الربوبية عن الكواكب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham sees the sun as it rises with daylight, in the very radiance his people claimed as divine.
rows.anchor: عند طلوع النهار وإشراق النور الذي ادعوا فيه ما ادعوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The masculine demonstrative for the feminine sun has a grammatical warrant; it magnifies her to disarm suspicion and signals from the outset that the feminine cannot be divine.
rows.anchor: وهو تذكير الخبر إظهارا لتعظيمها إبعادا عن التهمة , وتنبيها من أول الأمر على أن المؤنث لا يصلح للربوبية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone knows who strays from His path and who is guided; follow those He commands and avoid those He forbids, since He brings one astray and saves the other.
rows.anchor: يضل } أي يقع منه ضلال يوما ما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage recalls the pagan animal customs discussed here and in al-Ma'idah: despite God's gifts, people assigned shares of crops and livestock to powerless partners and withheld their blessings from their rightful owner.
rows.anchor: وكانوا مع ذلك قد كفروا نعمه تتعالى فاتخذوا معه شركاء ولم يكفهم ذلك حتى جعلوا لها مما ذرأ من الحرث والأنعام نصيبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'anic sequence affirms God's oneness through creation and its benefits, rebukes association, then commands eating what God created to recall the blessing and prompt gratitude.
rows.anchor: يذكر نفسه الشريفة بالوحدانية . ويستدل على ذلك بخلق السماوات والأرض وما أودع فيهما لنا من المنافع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This surah repeats the same sequence: God's splitting the grain follows Abraham's turning to the Creator, and the discussion then condemns making jinn partners with God.
rows.anchor: فالق الحب والنوى } ) 77 [ الأنعام : 95 ] بعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earlier example from al-Baqarah places God's creation of the heavens and earth before condemning those who take rivals and then commanding people to eat lawful food.
rows.anchor: إن في خلق السماوات والأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because God owns and rules everything and alone judges, the guided should eat what is lawful and named with His name; following His instruction means following the one who knows truth.
rows.anchor: فكلوا مما ذكر } أي وقت الذبح { اسم الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording indicates that actually invoking God's name over food is recommended.
rows.anchor: ليفهم أن الذكر بالفعل مندوب إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command concerns food eligible under God's law for His name to be invoked: lawful animal or other food, whether or not pagans had dedicated it to idols.
rows.anchor: كلوا مما يقبل أن يسمى عليه على مقتضى ما شةعه , وذلك هو الذي أحله من الحيوان وغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It excludes carrion, food named over with another's name, and intrinsically forbidden food, which invocation cannot make lawful.
rows.anchor: دون ما مات من الحيوان حتف أنفه , أو ذكر عليه اسم غير الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse urges people not to abstain from God's lawful crops and livestock merely because pagans named them for idols, and encourages invoking God's name over all lawful food.
rows.anchor: ولا تتبعوا المشركين في منعهم أنفسهم من خير مما خلق الله لهم من الحرث والأنعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-An'am gives a longer account than al-Baqarah because it is the surah of detailed explanation and argument for the implications of its claims.
rows.anchor: وإنما أطال هنا دون البقرة ما بين الجمل الكلام تقريرا لمضامينها وما يستتبعه واحتجاجا على جميع ذلك لأنها سورة التفصيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The condition of belief covers God's signs generally, including the laws of what is lawful and forbidden.
rows.anchor: بآياته } أي عامة التي منها آيات التحليل والتحريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question challenges why people would not eat lawful food bearing God's name when He has clarified prohibitions; necessity removes the specific restriction and restores the general baseline.
rows.anchor: إلا ما اضطررتم إليه } أي فإن الضرورة تزيل التفصيل عنه برده إلى ما كان عليه قبل التفصيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The meaning of the prior clarification depends on the audience: the first hearers had the forthcoming verse and earlier Meccan revelation, including recited or non-recited Prophetic revelation; later audiences have the ordered rulings of al-Baqarah, al-Ma'idah, and earlier surahs.
rows.anchor: والمراد في هذه الآية مختلف باختلاف المخاطبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since even food that could be named over may be forbidden through another's ownership or uncertainty, the command to leave sin covers both known prohibitions and concealed doubtful matters.
rows.anchor: ظاهر الإثم } أي المعلوم الحرمة من هذا وغيره { وباطنه } من كل ما فيه شبهة من الأقوال والأفعال والعقائد

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet defines sin as what unsettles the heart and wavers in the breast; Muslim transmits it from the Companion al-Nawwas ibn Sam'an.
rows.anchor: قال صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( والإثم ما حاك في القلب وتردد في الصدر )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Acquiring sin includes even its subtlest forms, including inward belief, as the bare verb indicates.
rows.anchor: إن الذين يكسبون الإثم } أي ولو بأخفى أنواع الكسب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive promise that sinners will be repaid has no possibility of failing, and should make the prudent fear any recompense.
rows.anchor: سيجزون } أي بوعد لا خلف فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The intensive verb form suggests evil acts require the self to struggle against its original sound disposition.
rows.anchor: وصيغة الافتعال للدلالة على أن أفعال الشر إنما تكون بمعالجة من النفس للفطرة الأولى السليمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The specific prohibition contrasts with the prior beneficial command: eating this food harms bodies and character.
rows.anchor: نهيا جازما خاصا عن الأكل مما يضرهم في أبدانهم وأخلاقهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He interprets food over which God's name was not mentioned as food that cannot accept the name because God prohibited it; it is impure in substance or meaning.
rows.anchor: فصار نجس العين أو المعنى , فصار مخبثا للبدن والنفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elsewhere, fisq is explained as food dedicated to other than God, and the same ruling covers carrion and other forbidden food; invoking God's name over it does not purify it.
rows.anchor: وتفسير الفسق في آية أخرى بما أهل به لغير الله وكذا ما كان في معناه مما مات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lawful food over which neither God's name nor another name was said remains lawful, as supported by the report from Aisha.
rows.anchor: وأما ما كان حلالا ولم يذكر عليه اسم الله ولا غيره فهو حلال

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: When people unsure about slaughter invocation brought meat, the Prophet told them to invoke God's name themselves and eat; Aisha says they were recent converts.
rows.anchor: يا رسول الله ! إن هنا أقواما حديث عهد بشرك يأتوننا بلحمان لا ندري يذكرون اسم الله أم لا ! قال : ( اذكروا أنتم اسم الله

rows.speaker: البغوي
rows.claim: Al-Baghawi argues that if invocation were a condition of permissibility, uncertainty about it would bar eating just as uncertainty about the slaughter itself would.
rows.anchor: قال البغوي : ولو كانت التسمية شرطا للإباحة لكان الشك في وجودها مانعا من أكلها كالشك في أصل الذبح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse's fisq refers to food whose type or status makes it unlawful, not omission of invocation by forgetfulness; the forgetful person is not a sinner.
rows.anchor: والناسي ليس بفاسق - كما قاله البخاري

rows.speaker: البخاري
rows.claim: Al-Bukhari transmits from Aisha that the Prophet instructed people unsure whether God's name had been said over meat to invoke it themselves and eat; this supports lawful meat without requiring actual invocation.
rows.anchor: عن عائشة رضي الله عنها أن قوما قالوا للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : إن قوما يأتونا باللحم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The devils' whisper is fast and forceful, aimed at allies whose similar natures make them receptive, so they will argue people away from God's command.
rows.anchor: ليوحون } أي يوسوسون وسوسة بالغة سريعة { إلى أوليائهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One argument claimed carrion killed by God was more fit to eat than animals slaughtered by people or their trained animals.
rows.anchor: بأن يقولوا لكم : ما قتله الله أحق بالأكل مما قتلتموه أنتم وجوارحكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other arguments included taboos about sanctuary boundaries, clothing during circumambulation, and vows to idols, all built on whim that the pagans themselves acknowledged as misleading and harmful.
rows.anchor: من خرافاتهم التي بنوا أمرهم فيها على الهوى الذي هم معترفون بأنه مضل مضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's prohibition alone is sufficient to demolish these arguments in general.
rows.anchor: ويكفي في هدم جميع شبههم إجمالا أن صاحب الدين ومالك الملك منع منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Obeying pagans in refusing food named for God, eating food unnamed for Him, or any dispute they raise means joining them in shirk, as when another deity is invoked over a sacrifice.
rows.anchor: إنكم لمشركون * } أي فأنتم وهم في الإشراك سواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an's rebuke of taking rabbis and monks as lords means people obeyed them by accepting their declarations of lawful and forbidden; religious names follow their underlying meanings.
rows.anchor: من أن عبادتهم لهم تحليلهم ما أحلوا وتحريمهم ما حرموا

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafi'i's explicit position is that a slaughter by a person of the Book in the name of someone other than God, such as Christ, is unlawful.
rows.anchor: عن نص الشافعي أنه لو كان لأهل الكتاب ذبيحة يذبحونها باسم غير الله كالمسيح لم تحل

rows.speaker: القاضي ابن كنج
rows.claim: Ibn Kanj rules forbidden a Jew's slaughter for Moses or a Christian's for Jesus or the cross.
rows.anchor: وفي كتاب القاضي ابن كنج أن اليهودي لو ذبح لموسى والنصراني لعيسى عليهما السلام أو للصليب حرمت ذبيحته

rows.speaker: القاضي ابن كنج
rows.claim: Ibn Kanj says a Muslim slaughtering for the Kaaba or the Messenger should be ruled forbidden because it is for other than God.
rows.anchor: وأن المسلم لو ذبح للكعبة أو لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فينبغي أن يقال : تحرم

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن
rows.claim: Abu al-Hasan gives a contrary view: the Muslim's slaughter for the Kaaba or Messenger is lawful because the Muslim slaughters for God and does not hold Christian beliefs about Jesus.
rows.anchor: وخرج أبو الحسن وجها آخر أنها تحل لأن المسلم يذبح لله ولا يعتقد في رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: القاضي ابن كنج
rows.claim: Slaughter for an idol is unlawful whether the slaughterer is Muslim or Christian.
rows.anchor: وإذا ذبح للصنم لم تؤكل ذبيحته سواء كان الذابح مسلما أو نصرانيا

rows.speaker: أهل بخارى
rows.claim: Ibrahim al-Marwazi records the Bukhara scholars' ruling that slaughtering for the ruler at his arrival is forbidden as an offering to other than God.
rows.anchor: أن ما يذبح عند استقبال السلطان تقربا إليه أفتى أهل بخارى بتحريمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author equates slaughter in a deity's name with prostration to it: both are forms of worship and particular acts of honor owed only to God.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن الذبح للمعبود باسمه نازل منزلة السجود له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Slaughtering an animal or object for another being as worship is unlawful and unbelief, including when the sacrifice is shared with God.
rows.anchor: فمن ذبح لغيره من حيوان أو جماد كالصنم على وجه التعظيم والعبادة لم تحل ذبيحته , وكان فعله كفرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A non-worshipful sacrifice for the Kaaba as God's house or for the Messenger should not invalidate the meat's permissibility.
rows.anchor: بأن ضحى أو ذبح للكعبة تعظيما لها لأنها بيت الله تعالى أو لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فهذا لا يجوز أن يمنع حل الذبيحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A ruler-arrival sacrifice expressing joy is like the aqiqah at a child's birth and does not entail unbelief; similarly, prostration can mean humility or submission.
rows.anchor: ومثل هذا لا يوجب الكفر , وكذا السجود لغير الله تذللا وخضوعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying God's name together with Muhammad's is not forbidden if the intention is to slaughter in God's name and seek blessing through Muhammad; the wording may still be disliked.
rows.anchor: إذا قال الذابح : بسم الله واسم محمد , وأراد : أذبح باسم الله وأتبرك باسم محمد , فينبغي أن لا يحرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition claimed by some can be understood as disapproval of the phrase itself, since a disliked act can be described as impermissible in the absolute sense.
rows.anchor: وقول من قال : لا يجوز ذلك , يمكن أن يحمل على أن اللفظ مكروه , لأن المكروه يصح نفي الجواز والإباحة المطلقة عنه

rows.speaker: الرافعي
rows.claim: Al-Rafi'i says the correct resolution of the dispute is the distinction set out above, and al-Nawawi cites supporting evidence.
rows.anchor: قال : والصواب ما بينا ؛ قال الشيخ محيي الدين

rows.speaker: صاحب التقريب
rows.claim: The author of al-Taqrib interprets the Christian naming Christ as slaughtering for Christ; mentioning Christ as a blessing on the Messenger is allowed.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب التقريب : معناه أن يذبحها له . فأما إن ذكر المسيح على معنى الصلاة على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فجائز

rows.speaker: الحليمي
rows.claim: Al-Halimi holds that the meat is lawful absolutely, even if the Christian names Christ.
rows.anchor: وقال الحليمي : تحل مطلقا وإن سمى المسيح

rows.speaker: ابن كج
rows.claim: Ibn Kajj allows slaughter for a person's satisfaction because the act is not thereby directed to that person, unlike an offering to an idol.
rows.anchor: قال ابن كج : من ذبح شاة وقال : أذبح لرضى فلان , حلت الذبيحة

rows.speaker: الروياني
rows.claim: Al-Ruyani allows slaughter to ward off jinn harm when seeking God's protection, but forbids it when the sacrifice is intended for the jinn.
rows.anchor: وقال الروياني : إن من ذبح للجن وقصد به التقرب إلى الله تعالى ليصرف شرهم عنه فهو حلال
